# `checkv-pyhmmer`

```{image} ../_static/supplementary_figures_checkv.svg
:width: 100%
:class: no-scaled-link
:align: center
```

CheckV-PyHMMER is a high-performance, memory-efficient implementation of the original CheckV software, optimized for speed and scalability through three key architectural changes: decoupling CPU-intensive modules from memory-intensive ones, replacing Prodigal with the parallelized Pyrodigal-gv to improve giant virus support, and substituting standard HMMER with the multi-threaded PyHMMER to enhance parallel processing. These enhancements allow for significantly faster analysis while maintaining over 99.9% output parity with the original CheckV—with minor differences arising only from the increased sensitivity of Pyrodigal-gv in identifying proteins—and users requiring the original implementation can revert to it using the `--checkv-original` flag.

vomix-snakemake can further implement a data-split functionality to both CheckV and CheckV-PyHMMER to reduce memory efficiency via the `--checkv-splits` configuration:

```{image} ../_static/supplementary_figures_splits.svg
:width: 100%
:class: no-scaled-link
:align: center
```

## Quick Run

::::{tab-set}
:::{tab-item} Single Fasta

**`Conda`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="checkv-pyhmmer" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`Apptainer`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="checkv-pyhmmer" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Conda)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="checkv-pyhmmer" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Apptainer)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="checkv-pyhmmer" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

:::
::::

``` {admonition} Dry Run
:class: Tip
Use the `-n` flag with your command to perform a dry-run first, listing all analyses that will be performed 
```

## Configuration

- **`checkv-original`:** Flag to use CheckV original instead of the much faster version in vOMIX-MEGA, CheckV-PyHMMER (default: "")
- **`checkv-splits`:** Number of input data splits for CheckV or CheckV-PyHMMER analysis, splitting data into n+1 chunks. Higher values reduce memory usage but increase runtime. Set to 0 for no splitting. (default: 0)
- **`checkv-params`:** Additional parameters to pass on to CheckV <https://bitbucket.org/berkeleylab/CheckV/src>. (default: "")
- **`checkv-database`:** Path to CheckV's database. (default: "workflow/database/checkv")

## Outputs

```bash
identify/viral/output/checkv
├── combined_classification_results.csv
├── complete_genomes.tsv
├── completeness.tsv
├── contamination.tsv
└── tmp
    ├── aai.tsv
    ├── diamond_checkpoint
    ├── diamond.tsv
    ├── diamond.tsv.cmd
    ├── diamond.tsv.log
    ├── gene_features.tsv
    ├── hmmsearch
    ├── hmmsearch_checkpoint
    ├── hmmsearch.txt
    ├── input_validation_checkpoint
    ├── proteins.faa
    └── tr.fna        
```

The main output from this module is the assembly file `final.contigs.fa` which includes the final contigs generated by `megahit` or `SPAdes`. These contigs will be used for many steps in downstream analysis.
